comments.author: Aharon Adams
comments.text:
full on diag attack with Devin. testing multiple plugs, testing against the Gtv, etc etc. ended up removing the rear box and changing plate to find the connectors had either fallen off and arced on the dc side when they did so. or they were blown off. tbd.
after removal of the rear box. as I was lifting up the charge plate to inspect the charger itself I found both high voltage connectors undone and laying next to it. charge port connector and DC conbox connector.
the conbox side appears to have either been blown off or at least arced when it finally fell off.
my running theory now is that both high voltage connectors were very loosely connected, just enough to let everything work and charge but slowly working their way off. when I sat in the car it finally moved it just enough to knock the DC side off which arced and pulled the charge port side off with it as the harnesses are touching each other where they live in the charging area.
now, my only issue is why there was power. im wondering if we somehow had a calibration in it that left the charger contactor on at all times? or if the contactor failed last charge cycle and failed closed? not sure yet.

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Claude's input:
Let me dig into the comments on the most relevant tasks for the actual fixes.Here's what's turned up from other Ampere builds with similar AC complaints. The Kelly 63 Corvette job is the closest match to what you're seeing, and there are useful breadcrumbs from a few others.
Kelly 63 Corvette — the most directly relevant case (Aharon)
Initial symptom was high-side pressure way too high — same family of problem you have. What they found and fixed, in order:
Pressure sensor wiring swapped. Signal and ground were reversed on the high-side pressure switch connector. Aharon repinned it and upgraded to the newer-style connector. This alone causes wildly wrong pressure readings to the VCU and would explain a fan that only triggers at unrealistic gauge values.
Bad pressure sensor reading. Earlier, Billy and Devin swapped the sensor and saw "weird readings" even with no pressure on it. Devin sent results back to Ampere. Worth eyeballing what the Ampere kPa readout says vs your manifold gauge.
Condenser/drier restriction. Billy noted the gauge high-side before the condenser was high, but Ampere read ~115 psi lower after the condenser. They confirmed by trying to pull a vacuum and not being able to draw the high side down without opening a valve. Cross-checked against the Zero Labs Bronco, which only drops 2–4 psi across the condenser. They cleared blockages by blowing lines and the drier out with nitrogen, then replaced the drier.
Charge level. Final fill was 1.75 lb (Vintage Air recommendation is 1.8 lb). After all the above, "pressures always looked good" on a 30-min drive and 1.5 hr of running.
Kelly 63 Corvette – Troubleshoot AC issues
Vargas 66 Mustang — condenser fan didn't cycle (Justin)
Vacuum and nitrogen test were clean, filled to 1.8 lb, system came on with the Vintage Air switch, but fans did not cycle — flagged as a config issue for Devin to fix in the Ampere setup. Confirms that the fan on/off trigger pressures live in Ampere config and need to be set correctly per car. 300 psi on / 250 psi off is wildly outside spec and points strongly at either bad config values or bad sensor data feeding good config.
Vargas 66 Mustang – Charge and test system
McDonough 77 Esprit — fan tuning (David)
David explicitly logged "Continued HVAC tuning w/ Devin to achieve desired refrigerant pressures & condenser fan on/off temps." Earlier he had condenser fans running all the time at only 1.2 lb charge. Confirms the fan thresholds are tuned per build with Devin.
McDonough 77 Esprit – Charge and test AC system
Barton 59 Impala — schrader valve and reassurance (Noah)
System tested out at 25/175 psi, ~45°F vent in the shop, filled to 1.25 lb. They "thought we had an issue" with cycling, but after a few dozen cycles found nothing wrong. Also note: a loose low-side schrader valve was found and snugged — worth checking on yours since a slow leak skews the equilibrium.
Barton 59 Impala – Charge and test system
Your own Ferdman 66 Bus — for context
You filled to 1 lb 6 oz, found a mis-pinned heater contactor, and already flagged "cycling a bit. May need tuning."
Ferdman 66 Bus – Charge and test system
---What this points to for your current Ampere
Your fan-on/off pressures (300/250 psi) are not normal trigger points — those are catastrophic-protection numbers, not control numbers. Two things are most likely going on, possibly together:
Bad high-side pressure data into the VCU. Either the pressure sensor signal/ground are swapped at the connector (Kelly Corvette fix) or the sensor itself is reading low — both will keep the fan from triggering until real pressure is sky-high. Compare your manifold gauge reading to the Ampere kPa readout right now; if there's a big delta (Kelly had 115 psi delta), that's the smoking gun.
Condenser or drier restriction. A real pressure drop across the condenser of more than a few psi means flow restriction. You can replicate Billy's test: shut it down, try to pull the high side into vacuum. If you can't draw it down without opening the manifold valve, there's a blockage. Reference Bronco was 2–4 psi drop across the condenser.
Secondary things to check based on history: condenser fan PMU output configuration (Devin owns this — has been a config issue on Vargas Mustang and Esprit), low-side schrader valve tightness (Barton Impala), and overall charge weight vs Vintage Air's 1.8 lb spec.
Recommend looping in Devin and Aharon — they're the ones who closed the Corvette case and own the Ampere fan-pressure configuration.
Sources:
Kelly 63 Corvette – Troubleshoot AC issues
Vargas 66 Mustang – Charge and test system
McDonough 77 Esprit – Charge and test AC system
Barton 59 Impala – Charge and test system
Ferdman 66 Bus – Charge and test system

Here's the suspension update for Ferdman: @Alex Noonan @Marc Davis @Ryan Laurel

Wheel clearance issue appears resolved from my limited test driving on Friday. The random narrowed beam Vintage V-dubs sent us at the beginning of the build fit with minor modification, however the drop was significant combined with the modified drop spindles the car came with (which was only caught when we sent them to be rebuilt). Due the maxed out height adjustment, the front end seems fairly stiff. When we get it driving more we'll be able to decide if this constitutes an issue.
The new beam does not have a provision for the OEM steering damper, which seems pretty common for adjustable beams. Would be easy to add later if we decide the steering needs it.

Issue:
When in R or D (inverter in PWM mode), high-pitched interference noise comes from speakers.

Diagnosis:
Beginning of diagnosis:
Noise isolated to rear.
Channel 1/2 and 3/4 filter settings both set to off.

Attempted to snuff with inline filters - no change.
Groudned inline filters per instructions - some modulation, but not eliminated.
Traced rear interference noise to channel 3 (nominally rear left)

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Ordering an iphone-to-RCA adapter to eliminate the RCA cable length/style as the issue, one less variable.
Ordering ferrite filters as an experiment.
Material matters more than size
Type 31 mix — best for 1–300 MHz, but also reasonably effective down to ~1 MHz. Good general-purpose choice for mixed noise.
Type 43 mix — the workhorse. Effective from ~25 MHz to 300 MHz. Most clamp-on chokes you'll find at car audio shops are Type 43.
Type 75 or 77 mix — better for lower frequencies (~10 kHz to 1 MHz). This is what you actually want for inverter switching noise on power lines.
Type 61 — higher frequency stuff, less useful here.
For a Hyper9/X1 setup, I'd reach for Type 31 or Type 75 mix for the 12V power lines feeding the amp, and Type 43 for the RCA signal lines.
Physical size — match to the cable
The cable should fit snugly through the bore. Air gaps kill effectiveness.
RCA cables (5–7mm OD): Fair-Rite 0431164281 (Type 43, ~0.5" ID) or similar small clamp-ons. Wrap the RCA through it 2–3 times if you have slack — each pass through multiplies impedance by N².
Amp +12V power (4–8 AWG, 10–15mm OD): Larger clamp-ons like Fair-Rite 0431167281 or 0443167251. For really fat power cables, look at the Würth 742 711 32 or DigiKey's larger split-core options.
